To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
students' writing development is connected to the genres of their social world, and the social institutions of their world are interconnected by genres.
The more a student is involved in the social action of the discipline, the more he or she learns to write in ways appropriate to that discipline.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how writing works as a tool for mediating human action in the world.
the social action that is carried out through the use of genres.
the ways people typify and use writing to mediate/construct their worlds together, and the ways those world intersect dynamically with schooling and other social institutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the article "Genre as Social action" is an attempt to bring together two traditions in composition and rhetoric: the North American tradition that has been concerned with genre and writing and the European tradition concerned with the social and historical dimensions of human activity.

the concept of typification in Schutz and Vygotsky has been an extremely useful tool for understanding how people use writing as a tool for social activity, and how that writing is connected to schooling, and that this understanding has been useful for thinking about how to use writing to support students in learning to act in the social institutions of the world.

genre as social action is a way of looking at writing and writing development that is grounded in the phenomenological sociology of Alfred Schutz, and that it is a way of connecting writing and writing development to human development and schooling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are still working to understand the relation between the individual and society, between the psychological and the sociological, between the cognitive and the social, in the ways we use writing to do things in the world together.
genre is the way we perceive and typify the world in terms that make it possible to act in it together, and that we learn to perceive and typify it through schooling.
genres are the way people typify writing as tool mediated social action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genre is a key concept in understanding the relation between schooling (and its genres) and the social institutions beyond schooling.

we need to understand genre in the context of social action, and that means we need to understand social action in the context of schooling, and that in turn means we need to look at the whole range of social action beyond schooling.
we need to understand how people typify the world around them and the texts that mediate their action in it.
